questions.question: Which of the following statements about methods are true? (Choose all that apply.)

choices.A: Overloaded methods must have the same signature.
choices.B: Overridden methods must have the same signature.
choices.C: Hidden methods must have the same signature.
choices.D: Overloaded methods must have the same return type.
choices.E: Overridden methods must have the same return type.
choices.F: Hidden methods must have the same return type.

questions.explanation: Overloaded methods have the same method name but a different signature (the method parameters differ), making option A incorrect. Overridden instance methods and hidden static methods must have the same signature (the name and method parameters must match), making options B and C correct. Overloaded methods can have different return types, while overridden and hidden methods can have covariant return types. None of these methods are required to use the same return type, making options D, E, and F incorrect.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about overridden methods are true? (Choose all
     that apply.)

choices.A:
An overridden method must contain method parameters that are the same or covariant
        with the method parameters in the inherited method.
choices.B: An overridden method may declare a new exception, provided it is not checked.
choices.C: An overridden method must be more accessible than the method in the parent class.
choices.D:
An overridden method may declare a broader checked exception than the method in the
         parent class.
choices.E:
If an inherited method returns void, then the overridden version of the method must
         return void.
choices.F: None of the above

questions.explanation:
The signature must match exactly, making option A incorrect. There is no such thing as
    a covariant signature. An overridden method must not declare any new checked exceptions
    or a checked exception that is broader than the inherited method. For this reason, option B is
     correct, and option D is incorrect. Option C is incorrect because an overridden method may
    have the same access modifier as the version in the parent class. Finally, overridden methods
    must have covariant return types, and only void is covariant with void, making option
   E correct.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about inheritance are correct? (Choose all that apply.)

choices.A: A class can directly extend any number of classes.
choices.B: A class can implement any number of interfaces.
choices.D: If class A is extended by B, then B is a superclass of A.
choices.E: If class C implements interface D, then C is a subtype of D.
choices.F: Multiple inheritance is the property of a class to have multiple direct superclasses.

questions.explanation:
A class can only directly extend a single class, making option A incorrect. A class can
    implement any number of interfaces, though, making option B correct. Option C is incor-
     rect because primitive variables types do not inherit java.lang.Object. If a class extends
    another class, then it is a subclass, not a superclass, making option D incorrect. A class that
    implements an interface is a subtype of that interface, making option E correct. Finally,
    option F is correct as it is an accurate description of multiple inheritance, which is not per-
    mitted in Java.

questions.question: Which of the following are true? (Choose all that apply.)

choices.A: this() can be called from anywhere in a constructor.
choices.B: this() can be called from anywhere in an instance method.
choices.C: this.variableName can be called from any instance method in the class.
choices.D: this.variableName can be called from any static method in the class.
choices.E: You can call the default constructor written by the compiler using this().
choices.F: You can access a private constructor with the main() method in the same class.

questions.explanation:
Calling an overloaded constructor with this() may be used only as the first line of a
     constructor, making options A and B incorrect. Accessing this.variableName can be per-
    formed from any instance method, constructor, or instance initializer, but not from a static
    method or static initializer. For this reason, option C is correct, and option D is incorrect.
    Option E is tricky. The default constructor is written by the compiler only if no user-defined
    constructors were provided. And this() can only be called from a constructor in the same
     class. Since there can be no user-defined constructors in the class if a default constructor was
     created, it is impossible for option E to be true. Since the main() method is in the same
     class, it can call private methods in the class, making option F correct.

questions.question: Which of the following are properties of immutable classes? (Choose all that apply.)

choices.A: The class can contain setter methods, provided they are marked final.
choices.B: The class must not be able to be extended outside the class declaration.
choices.C: The class may not contain any instance variables.
choices.D: The class must be marked static.
choices.E: The class may not contain any static variables.
choices.F: The class may only contain private constructors.
choices.G:
The data for mutable instance variables may be read, provided they cannot be modified
        by the caller.
                                                   Review Questions        341

questions.explanation: Immutable objects do not include setter methods, making option A incorrect. An immutable class must be marked final or contain only private constructors, so no subclass can extend it and make it mutable, making option B correct. Options C and E are incorrect, as immutable classes can contain both instance and static variables. Option D is incorrect, as marking a class static is not a property of immutable objects. Option F is incorrect. While an immutable class may contain only private constructors, this is not a requirement. Finally, option G is correct. It is allowed for the caller to access data in mutable elements of an immutable object, provided they have no ability to modify these elements.

      literals in Java are considered int by default. This constructor calls the Fox() constructor

     the correct pathway, but then execute them from the top down using the established order.

questions.question: Which of the following are true about a concrete class? (Choose all that apply.)

choices.A: A concrete class can be declared as abstract.
choices.B: A concrete class must implement all inherited abstract methods.
choices.C: A concrete class can be marked as final.
choices.D: A concrete class must be immutable.
choices.E:
A concrete method that implements an abstract method must match the method declara-
         tion of the abstract method exactly.

questions.explanation:
Concrete classes are, by definition, not abstract, so option A is incorrect. A concrete
     class must implement all inherited abstract methods, so option B is correct. Concrete classes
    can be optionally marked final, so option C is correct. Option D is incorrect; concrete
     classes need not be immutable. A concrete subclass only needs to override the inherited
     abstract method, not match the declaration exactly. For example, a covariant return type can
    be used. For this reason, option E is incorrect.
